name: Nothing Couloir

pitch_detail.notes: Shallow right fork, slabby class 3 climbing on clean rock.
Brief class 4 step moving right into a second couloir.
Sustained slabby class 3 to the ridge crest.
Summit ridge traverse south, around towers on the west side, with brief class 4 moves.

descent_text: Descend the South Shoulder route, which pairs well with the Nothing Couloir's west-side approach to form a natural loop back down toward Leroy Creek Basin rather than reversing the climb.
approach: Same lower approach as the North Face/Entiat Icefall routes: Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft) via FR 6211, up the Phelps Creek Trail to the Leroy Creek crossing, then the climber's trail into Leroy Creek Basin (~6,100-6,200 ft, ~5 miles), continuing onto the peak's west side to reach the base of the couloir system near the standard West/South Slopes route.
overview: A late-season class 3/4 rock scramble up a clean, solid-rock couloir system on Mount Maude's WNW side, the second gully right of the North Tower, finishing along the summit ridge with brief class 4 moves around towers.
beta: From the west side of the mountain, locate the couloir as the second gully to the right of the North Tower. Follow the shallow right fork up slabby class 3 rock, move right into another couloir with a brief class 4 step, then continue sustained slabby class 3 climbing to the ridge crest. From there, traverse south toward the main summit, passing around towers on the west (right) side with occasional brief class 4 moves.
gear: optional rope/rack for parties uncomfortable soloing class 4
fa: Uncertain: possibly Hermann Ulrichs and John Burnett, July 1932, or Leland Windham, September 6, 2001
face: WNW side (second gully right of the North Tower)
